correctness.rationale: In any proper coloring center c is fresh and each outer edge has two distinct endpoint colors. Each outer vertex automatically meets odd neighborhood counts because it sees distinct center and partner colors. At c, each outer color has positive odd multiplicity <=k. There must be an even number q of outer colors; q=2 forces both sizes k and is possible iff k odd. For even 4<=q<=2k, choose positive odd class sizes d_i<=k summing to 2k by distributing k-q/2 units among q capacities floor((k-1)/2); capacity is sufficient. A complete multipartite graph with these classes has a perfect matching because largest part <=k, placing distinct colors at each edge. This proves all allowed counts for every k>=2. Independent canonical partition enumeration gave F2:{5}, F3:{3,5,7}, F4:{5,7,9}.
